overview.title: 📖 Overview: Which Female Animals Carry Real Sanctity
overview.subtitle: Temurah 20a–20b
overview.hebrewSource: שֶׁאֵין לְךָ דָּבָר עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה, אֶלָּא הָרוֹעֶה לְהִסְתָּאֵב
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Rabbi Shimon rules that a female animal designated for a burnt offering can generate a substitute, but one designated for a Paschal or guilt offering cannot — since only an animal that must genuinely graze until blemished (rather than being sold immediately) carries the inherent sanctity temurah requires. Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi partly disagrees regarding the Paschal offering, since its leftover becomes a peace offering (open to females) — but not regarding the guilt offering, whose leftover funds only communal gifts, which never generate temurah. The Gemara tests Rabbi Shimon's logic against tricky cases (a High Priest's substitute cow, a king's or individual's mismatched goat) before turning to a new mishna about the endless line of a guilt offering's substitute, and a debate — reversed, then reversed again — about whether that line can be sacrificed before or only after the original guilt offering achieves atonement.

slides.title: 🐏 Which Female-Designated Animals Make a Substitute?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Shimon's principle, and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's partial dissent

lines.speaker: Rabbi Shimon
lines.text: A female designated for a BURNT offering makes temurah (since a female bird burnt offering exists). But for a PASCHAL or GUILT offering — no temurah, since it may be sold immediately, without waiting for a blemish.

lines.speaker: Principle
lines.text: 'No animal generates a substitute except one that must graze to become blemished' — real inherent sanctity is required.

lines.speaker: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
lines.text: I disagree about the Paschal offering: since a LEFTOVER Paschal animal becomes a peace offering (open to females), the mother has real sanctity and SHOULD make a substitute.

lines.speaker: But not the guilt offering
lines.text: A leftover guilt offering's proceeds fund only COMMUNAL gift offerings — and a community can never perform temurah, so this case stays as Rabbi Shimon ruled.

callout.label: Key contrast:
callout.text: The Paschal leftover becomes an INDIVIDUAL peace offering (open to females); the guilt leftover becomes a COMMUNAL offering (which can't generate temurah anyway) — hence the different outcomes.

slides.title: 🧩 Stress-Testing Rabbi Shimon's Logic
slides.subtitle: Three tricky counter-cases, each resolved the same way

nodes.content: ❓ A High Priest designates a COW instead of his bull for Yom Kippur — shouldn't it be sanctified, since the red heifer (a sin-offering-like animal) is female?
💬 No — the red heifer is bedek habayit (Temple upkeep) sanctity, not altar sanctity; bedek habayit never makes temurah
❓ An individual designates a MALE goat for his (female) sin offering — the king's goat sin offering is male, so shouldn't this count?
❓ Or a KING designates a female goat — an individual's sin offering IS female, so shouldn't THAT count?
✅ No to both — a king and an ordinary individual are 'two distinct bodies' (different classes of obligation); one's offering-status can't transfer to the other's mismatched case

callout.label: The recurring answer:
callout.text: Status only counts as 'existing for the mother' when it belongs to a case that could genuinely apply to THIS specific person and situation — not merely to someone else in a similar role.

slides.title: 📦 Consecrating 'All My Possessions' — What Happens to the Animals?
slides.subtitle: A related mishna on unspecified consecration, with its own dispute

boxes.title: Rabbi Eliezer
items: Assumes bedek habayit (Temple upkeep) was intended by default
Males sold for burnt-offering use; females sold for peace-offering use
All proceeds go to Temple maintenance

boxes.title: Rabbi Yehoshua
items: Males THEMSELVES sacrificed as burnt offerings; females sold for peace-offering use, proceeds fund burnt offerings
Only non-sacrificial property goes to Temple maintenance

callout.label: The puzzle for Rabbi Yehoshua:
callout.text: If the females were consecrated with burnt-offering intent (deferred sanctity, since females can't be burnt offerings), how can they simply be sold and used for a DIFFERENT purpose (peace offerings)? Rabbi Yoḥanan resolves this by aligning Rabbi Yehoshua with the view that female-for-burnt-offering carries no inherent sanctity at all (per an alternate version of Rabbi Shimon's own position).

slides.title: 📋 New Mishna: The Guilt Offering's Substitute-Line
slides.subtitle: Three positions on animals descended from a guilt offering's temurah
rows: Graze until blemished, sold, proceeds fund COMMUNAL gift offerings
Left to die (not sold at all)
Graze until blemished, sold, but proceeds fund an INDIVIDUAL burnt offering (with semikha, libations, hide rights — unlike communal offerings)
Why both disputed cases are needed

Guilt offering after atonement alone might suggest a special decree just for THAT case; substitute-line alone might suggest leniency since it was never eligible to begin with — each needs its own teaching

callout.label: Real difference between Rabbi Elazar and the Rabbis:
callout.text: An individual offering requires the owner's hands (semikha), his own libations, and (if he's a priest) his own share of hide and service — a communal offering has none of these personal elements.

slides.title: ⏳ Before or After Atonement — Reversed Twice
slides.subtitle: Rav Naḥman's report, Rava's objections, and the corrected version

lines.speaker: First version
lines.text: Rav Naḥman (citing Rabba bar Avuh): the dispute applies only AFTER atonement; BEFORE atonement, everyone agrees the offspring itself can be sacrificed as a guilt offering.

lines.speaker: Rava objects
lines.text: Two problems: (1) one cannot achieve atonement through an item that came from a transgression (the substitute was created through a forbidden act); (2) a supporting baraita shows only the FIRST offspring is ever sacrificed — this offspring is already 'second-generation,' descended from a substitute!

lines.speaker: Corrected version
lines.text: Actually: the dispute applies only BEFORE atonement (should it graze, or die, out of concern it might still be wrongly offered as a guilt offering?); AFTER atonement, everyone agrees it's sacrificed as a burnt offering, since that concern no longer applies.

lines.speaker: Same objection returns
lines.text: But Rav Ḥananya's baraita (only the first offspring is ever sacrificed) STILL contradicts this corrected version too! The difficulty (קַשְׁיָא) stands unresolved.

callout.label: Open question:
callout.text: The daf ends without fully reconciling how the 'only first offspring is sacrificed' principle fits with either version of the before/after-atonement distinction.

summary.principle: Only an animal with real inherent sanctity — one that must graze until blemished rather than being sold immediately — can generate a substitute, and this same requirement runs through mismatched-sex consecrations, unspecified property consecration, and the extended line descended from a guilt offering's own substitute.

flowSteps.content: 🐏 R' Shimon: female-for-olah makes temurah; female-for-pesach/asham does not — R' Yehuda HaNasi partly dissents on Pesach
🧩 Tricky counter-cases (Kohen Gadol's cow, mismatched goats) all resolved: status must belong to the SAME person's situation

columns.content: 📦 Unspecified consecration: bedek habayit default (R' Eliezer) vs. burnt-offering default (R' Yehoshua)
📋 Guilt offering's substitute-line: graze/communal (Rabbis), die (R' Eliezer), or individual burnt offering (R' Elazar)

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: temurah requires genuine inherent sanctity — an animal merely destined for immediate, unblemished sale never generates a substitute

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, why does he disagree with Rabbi Shimon specifically regarding a female designated for a PASCHAL offering (but not a guilt offering)?
o: He disagrees with Rabbi Shimon on both cases equally

A leftover Paschal offering becomes an individual peace offering (open to females), giving the mother real sanctity; a leftover guilt offering funds only communal gifts, which can't generate temurah anyway
Paschal offerings are always male
He agrees fully with Rabbi Shimon on everything
quiz.e: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi distinguishes the two cases based on what the 'leftover' offering becomes: a peace offering (individual, female-eligible) for Pesach, versus communal gifts (never eligible for temurah) for a guilt offering.

quiz.q: Why doesn't a king's female goat sin offering count as having 'sin offering' status when an individual designates a male goat instead of his own required female?
o: Because kings never sin
Because a king and an ordinary individual are considered 'two distinct bodies' — one's offering type cannot transfer status to the other's mismatched case
Because goats can never be sin offerings
Because the Gemara rejects the entire premise
quiz.e: The Gemara explains that offering-status must belong to a case that could genuinely apply to the SAME person's situation; a king's male goat and an individual's female goat belong to different categories of people and cannot cross-validate each other.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yehoshua's opinion on consecrating all one's possessions, what happens to males that are fit for sacrifice?
o: They are sold for Temple maintenance only
They are sacrificed as burnt offerings themselves
They are always left to graze
They are given to the poor
quiz.e: Rabbi Yehoshua holds that since burnt-offering intent is assumed by default, fit males are sacrificed directly as burnt offerings, while females (which can't be burnt offerings) are sold to fund burnt offerings.

quiz.q: According to the new mishna, what is Rabbi Elazar's position on the money from selling a guilt offering's substitute-line (once blemished)?
o: The money is simply forfeited
The money funds an INDIVIDUAL burnt offering, with the owner's semikha, libations, and (if a priest) hide rights
The money funds a communal gift offering, like the Rabbis say
The animals are never sold at all
quiz.e: Rabbi Elazar holds the proceeds fund an individual burnt offering — distinct from the Rabbis' view of a communal gift offering, which lacks semikha, personal libations, and individual hide/service rights.

quiz.q: What two objections does Rava raise against the first version of Rav Naḥman's statement (that before atonement, everyone agrees the offspring can be sacrificed directly)?
o: There are no objections; Rava agrees fully
One cannot achieve atonement via an item from a transgression, and a supporting baraita shows only the FIRST offspring (not this 'second-generation' one) is ever sacrificed
Rava says the mishna doesn't exist
Rava says only priests can raise this question
quiz.e: Rava objects that the substitute's offspring stems from a forbidden act (disqualifying it from achieving atonement) and that Rav Ḥananya's baraita limiting sacrifice to only the first offspring contradicts sacrificing this twice-removed offspring.
